nodes.name: NiCo@ZIF-8 Precursor Formation
nodes.procedure: Ni and Co atoms were encapsulated in the cage of ZIF-8 as guests due to the atom size matching (2.5Å atoms vs 3.4Å pores and 11.6Å cavity), while ZIF-8 served as active sites host using the MOF-assisted host-guest strategy.
nodes.source_text: We successfully synthesized Ni/Co DASs anchored on N-doped carbon substrate (NiCo DASs/N-C) using the MOF-assisted host-guest strategy (Figure 1a). First, Ni and Co atoms with a diameter of 2.5Å were encapsulated in the cage of ZIF-8...

unit_operations.name: Atom Encapsulation
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: Ni and Co atoms with a diameter of 2.5Å were encapsulated in the cage of ZIF-8 as a guest due to the atom size matching, while the ZIF-8 served as active sites host with the pore size of 3.4Å and the cavity diameter of 11.6Å

nodes.name: NiCo DASs/N-C Pyrolysis
nodes.procedure: The NiCo@ZIF-8 precursor was pyrolyzed under N₂ at 920°C. With the evaporation of Zn atoms, ZIF-8 was carbonized to form N-C substrate to provide anchor sites, while the Ni-N₄ and Co-N₄ sites are uniformly embedded into 3D porous carbon substrate.
nodes.source_text: Then the NiCo@ZIF-8 precursor was pyrolyzed under N₂ at 920°C. With the evaporation of Zn atoms, ZIF-8 was carbonized to form N-C substrate...

unit_operations.name: Pyrolysis
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: The NiCo@ZIF-8 precursor was pyrolyzed under N₂ at 920°C

unit_operations.name: Carbonization
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: With the evaporation of Zn atoms, ZIF-8 was carbonized to form N-C substrate

nodes.name: Ni SAs/N-C Synthesis
nodes.procedure: Single-atomic Ni-N₄ site catalyst (Ni SAs/N-C) was synthesized using the MOF-assisted host-guest strategy similar to NiCo DASs/N-C but with only Ni atoms encapsulated in ZIF-8 followed by pyrolysis.
nodes.source_text: we also synthesized the single-atomic Ni-N₄ site catalyst (Ni SAs/N-C) for comparative study.

nodes.description: ORR performance in O₂-saturated 0.1 M KOH
nodes.source_text: The electrocatalytic ORR performance of all samples is investigated in O₂-saturated 0.1 M KOH... NiCo DASs/N-C electrocatalyst exhibits the outstanding half-wave potential (E₁/₂) (0.880 V)... smallest Tafel slopes of 82.7 mV dec⁻¹... H₂O₂ yield... remains below 2.5%... electron transfer number is 3.9-4... superior long-term stability with neglected change of polarization curve after 5000 continue CV cycles

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD spectra reveal only broad peaks ≈25° and 44° attributed to (002) and (101) crystal planes of graphite carbon, excluding formation of crystal metal species.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffraction patterns (XRD) spectra of NiCo DASs/N-C, Co SAs/N-C, and Ni SAs/N-C reveal only broad peaks ≈25° and 44° attributed to the (002) and (101) crystal planes of graphite carbon ... which further excludes the formation of crystal metal species.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman spectra show largest ID/IG value (1.25) for NiCo DASs/N-C, suggesting higher degree of defect.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Raman spectra of NiCo DASs/N-C show the largest ID/IG value (1.25) suggesting that the higher degree of defect for NiCo DASs/N-C catalyst.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM indicates NiCo DASs/N-C, Co SAs/N-C, and Ni SAs/N-C catalysts maintain rhombic dodecahedral morphology with no metal NPs observed.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscope (SEM) and transmission electron microscope (TEM) indicate that the NiCo DASs/N-C, Co SAs/N-C, and Ni SAs/N-C catalysts still remain the rhombic dodecahedral morphology, with no metal NPs observed.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows rhombic dodecahedral morphology with no metal NPs; SAED presents ring-like pattern indicating poor crystallinity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscope (SEM) and transmission electron microscope (TEM) indicate that the NiCo DASs/N-C, Co SAs/N-C, and Ni SAs/N-C catalysts still remain the rhombic dodecahedral morphology, with no metal NPs observed ... The selected area electron diffraction (SAED) profile of NiCo DASs/N-C catalyst presents a ring-like pattern, indicating poor crystallinity.

nodes.characterization_summary: AC-HAADF-STEM shows bright spots in pairs (red boxes) with distances ≈6.4Å demonstrating dual single atoms; HAADF-STEM mapping shows homogeneous Ni, Co, N, C distribution.
nodes.evidence_snippet: A large number of bright spots can be observed in the abbreviation-corrected high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (AC-HAADF-STEM) ... The enlarged AC-HAADF-STEM image shows that many bright spots come in pairs (typically circled by red boxes), suggesting dual single atoms exist in NiCo DASs/N-C.

nodes.characterization_summary: N2 adsorption-desorption isotherms show type IV isotherm; NiCo DASs/N-C has BET surface area 1225.1 m²g⁻¹, Ni SAs/N-C 428.9 m²g⁻¹, Co SAs/N-C 391.1 m²g⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The N2 adsorption-desorption isotherms suggest that NiCo DASs/N-C exhibits type IV isotherm with a larger Brunner-Emmet-Teller (BET) surface area (1225.1m²g⁻¹) than Ni SAs/N-C (428.9m²g⁻¹) and Co SAs/N-C (391.1m²g⁻¹).

nodes.characterization_summary: Co 2p3/2 shows 0.4 eV positive shift from Co SAs/N-C to NiCo DASs/N-C indicating lower Co valence; Ni 2p shows 0.4 eV negative shift indicating decreasing Ni oxidation state.
nodes.evidence_snippet: A noticeable 0.4eV positive shift of Co²⁺2p3/2 can be observed from the X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) of Co SAs/N-C to NiCo DASs/N-C ... From the Ni 2p spectra, the high valence Ni²⁺ exhibits a 0.4eV negative shift binding energy from Ni SAs/N-C to NiCo DASs/N-C.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co K-edge absorption edge between CoO and Co3O4 (valence +2 to +3); Ni K-edge between NiO and Ni foil (valence 0 to +2).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XANES of Co K-edge indicated that the absorption edge of NiCo DASs/N-C catalyst locates between CoO and Co3O4 demonstrating that the valence of Co element is between +2 and +3 ... The Ni adsorption edge of NiCo DASs/N-C catalyst is located between NiO and Ni foil, suggesting that the valence state of Ni element is between 0 and +2.

nodes.characterization_summary: FT-k³-weighted EXAFS shows only Co-N peak at 1.5Å and Ni-N peak at 1.31Å with no metal-metal coordination; coordination numbers Ni-N 4.2 and Co-N 4.0; no Ni-Co bond observed.
nodes.evidence_snippet: From the Co Fourier-transformed (FT) k³-weighted EXAFS curve of NiCo DASs/N-C, only one peak at 1.5Å can be observed in R space, which can be assigned to the Co-N coordination ... For the Ni FT-EXAFS curve of NiCo DASs/N-C, there is one main peak attributed to Ni-N coordination at 1.31Å ... the coordination number of Ni-N and Co-N are 4.2 and 4.0, respectively ... It is worth noting that the bond of Ni-Co is not observed.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman shows peaks at 605 cm⁻¹ (CoOOH), 500 cm⁻¹ (Co(OH)₂), 1150 cm⁻¹ (O-O stretching of O₂⁻), and 1048 cm⁻¹ (OH deformation); ID/IG ratio stable indicating high structural stability.
nodes.evidence_snippet: When increasing the potential to 0.808 V vs. RHE, the peak appears at 605 cm⁻¹ ascribed to CoOOH. With the applied voltage decreasing, the Raman peak at 500 cm⁻¹ attributed to Co(OH)₂ is formed ... an obvious Raman peak appeared near 1150 cm⁻¹ ... which can be attributed to the O-O stretching vibrations of superoxide O₂⁻.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ ATR-SEIRAS captures *O₂⁻ (~1100 cm⁻¹), *OOH (~1240 cm⁻¹), Co-O (1455 cm⁻¹), and O-H/H-O-H peaks, confirming dynamic O₂ activation and *OOH formation on Co-N₄ sites.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The absorption peaks of *O₂⁻ near 1100 cm⁻¹ and *OOH near 1240 cm⁻¹ begin to appear with the potential decreased ... a prominent peak at 1455 cm⁻¹ corresponds to Co-O double bond is observed, manifesting the formation of CoOOH intermediate.
